key_insight: In 2D model glasses under cyclic shear, fatigue life diverges near the fatigue limit with a ~-1 power-law exponent, showing dimensionality changes how failure time scales.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict fatigue failure in amorphous solids by linking accumulated plastic damage to eventual rupture, with implications for designing more durable materials.
method: Atomistic simulations of 2D glass under cyclic shear deformation
Measured cycles-to-failure as strain amplitude approached the fatigue limit
Used isoconfigurational seeded simulations with a localized soft region to probe failure variability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that cycles to failure follow a power-law divergence with exponent close to -1, while dissipated work and non-affine displacement scale consistently with failure time.
watch_item: The localized seeding constrains where failure occurs but does not remove the broad distribution of failure times, so predictions remain probabilistic rather than deterministic.
paper_title: Fatigue failure in two-dimensional glasses under cyclic shear deformation
